shared_context.topic: whether antibiotics prevent progression of Lyme disease

atoms.1: Antibiotics are effective in preventing the progression of Lyme disease if administered early in the course of the infection.
atoms.2: Early treatment of Lyme disease typically involves oral antibiotics.
atoms.3: Doxycycline is an oral antibiotic used for early treatment of Lyme disease.
atoms.4: Amoxicillin is an oral antibiotic used for early treatment of Lyme disease.
atoms.5: Cefuroxime axetil is an oral antibiotic used for early treatment of Lyme disease.
atoms.6: For early localized Lyme disease, a 10- to 21-day course of antibiotics is generally recommended.
atoms.7: For early disseminated Lyme disease, a 10- to 21-day course of antibiotics is generally recommended.
atoms.8: If Lyme disease is treated promptly, most patients recover completely without long-term complications.
atoms.9: If Lyme disease is not treated in its early stages, it can progress to more severe forms.
atoms.10: Severe forms of Lyme disease include Lyme arthritis.
atoms.11: Severe forms of Lyme disease include neurological Lyme disease.
atoms.12: Severe forms of Lyme disease include Lyme carditis.
atoms.13: In severe cases of Lyme disease, longer courses of antibiotics may be required.
atoms.14: In severe cases of Lyme disease, intravenous antibiotics may be required.

snippets.output: Antibiotics are effective in preventing the progression of Lyme disease if administered early in the course of the infection; early treatment of Lyme disease typically involves oral antibiotics such as doxycycline, amoxicillin, and cefuroxime axetil.
For early localized and early disseminated Lyme disease, a 10- to 21-day course of antibiotics is generally recommended.
If Lyme disease is treated promptly, most patients recover completely without long-term complications.

If Lyme disease is not treated in its early stages, it can progress to more severe forms, including Lyme arthritis, neurological Lyme disease, and Lyme carditis. In such cases of Lyme disease, longer courses of antibiotics or intravenous antibiotics may be required.
